What Is Sales Velocity?

Explainerlowob research

By Chris WellsFrom lowob RESEARCH · 28 September 2026 · 5-minute read · Revenue

Sales velocity is the revenue a sales pipeline produces per day. It multiplies the number of qualified opportunities by average deal size and win rate, then divides by the average sales cycle in days. The single number matters less than its four inputs: velocity shows which lever is moving, and lets a team test whether a change in one is worth a loss in another.

What sales velocity means

The formula, as set out in Pipedrive's guide:

Sales velocity = (number of opportunities × average deal size × win rate) ÷ sales cycle length in days

Each input has a precise meaning. Opportunities are qualified deals entering the pipeline in the period, not raw leads. Average deal size is total won value divided by the number of deals won. Win rate is the share of opportunities won. Cycle length is the average time from first contact to close.

Pipedrive's example uses 20 deals, a $5,000 average, a 40% win rate and a 60-day cycle. That gives $40,000 of expected won value divided by 60 days, or about $667 a day.

This is a different measure from selling time. What Is Selling Time? covers how much of a seller's week goes to customers. Velocity measures what the pipeline produces, whoever is working it.

Why it matters for a commercial team

Velocity is useful because the four levers trade against each other. Moving upmarket raises deal size but usually lengthens the cycle and lowers win rate. Tighter qualification cuts the number of opportunities but should raise win rate. Velocity shows the net effect.

The sensitivity is easy to see on Pipedrive's baseline:

Change (others held constant)New velocity per dayChange
Baseline$667none
Opportunities +10% (22)$733+10%
Deal size +10% ($5,500)$733+10%
Win rate +10% (44%)$733+10%
Cycle −10% (54 days)$741+11%
Cycle +25% (75 days)$533−20%

Recent data shows several levers moving at once. Ebsta and Pavilion's analysis of 4.2 million opportunities found win rates fell 18% and average deal values fell 21% in 2023 against 2022, while sales cycles grew 38% against 2021 before shortening towards the end of 2023. On the formula, falls of that size compound.

Buyer behaviour explains part of the cycle effect. Forrester's 2024 survey of more than 16,000 business buyers found 13 people on average involved in a buying decision, 89% of purchases involving two or more departments, and 86% of purchases stalling during the process. Gartner's 2026 survey of 646 buyers found 67% preferred a rep-free experience and 45% had used AI during a recent purchase. More stakeholders and more self-directed research tend to stretch the time from first contact to close.

How to use it without gaming it

Velocity is easy to inflate. Count unqualified leads as opportunities and it rises. Drop stalled deals from the win-rate denominator and it rises again. The safeguards are mostly about definitions.

InputCommon distortionSafeguard
OpportunitiesCounting leads or meetingsCount only deals past a written qualification stage
Deal sizeUsing list price or one large outlierUse median won value as a cross-check
Win rateExcluding no-decision lossesInclude closed-lost and no-decision in the denominator
Cycle lengthStarting the clock at opportunity creationStart at first meaningful contact, and state the rule

A practical routine for a 20 to 500 person firm:

  1. Calculate it by segment. New business and expansion, or mid-market and enterprise, usually have very different velocities.
  2. Track it monthly, on a trailing 12-month window. Short windows swing on single deals.
  3. Change one lever at a time. If the team tightens qualification, expect opportunities to fall and win rate to rise, and judge the change on the net.
  4. Write down the reason. When velocity moves, record which lever moved and why. That note is more useful next year than the figure itself.

In lowob's model, velocity is a reading of the commercial record. An assistant can calculate it in seconds, but it cannot fix stage definitions, missing loss reasons or rolling close dates. Those belong to whoever owns the record.

lowob takeaways

  • Four levers, one number. Velocity combines volume, deal size, win rate and cycle time.
  • Cycle length bites hardest. Shortening the cycle helps slightly more than an equal gain elsewhere, and lengthening it hurts more.
  • Definitions decide the figure. Loose qualification or excluded losses make velocity look better than it is.
  • Use it to compare trade-offs. Its main value is showing the net effect of changing one lever.

Common questions

How do you calculate sales velocity?

Multiply the number of qualified opportunities by average deal size and win rate, then divide by the average sales cycle in days. The result is revenue per day.

What is a good sales velocity?

There is no universal benchmark because it depends on deal size and segment. Compare your own figure over time and between segments.

How can I increase sales velocity?

Raise opportunity volume, deal size or win rate, or shorten the cycle. Tighter qualification often lifts win rate and shortens cycles at the cost of fewer opportunities.

What is the difference between sales velocity and pipeline coverage?

Coverage compares pipeline value with a target at a point in time. Velocity measures how fast pipeline converts into won revenue.

Sources and notes

  • Pipedrive, What Is Sales Velocity and How Do You Boost It?, September 2026. Vendor guide; source of the formula and worked example.
  • Ebsta and Pavilion, 2024 B2B Sales Benchmarks, 2024. Vendor dataset of 4.2 million opportunities across 530 companies.
  • Forrester, To Master B2B Buying Mayhem, Providers Must Prioritize Buyers' Needs, December 2024. Analyst press release; source of the 89% and 86% figures.
  • Forrester, The State Of Business Buying: Companies Still Struggle To Meet Buyer Expectations, December 2024, by Barbara Winters. Analyst blog; survey of more than 16,000 global business buyers.
  • Gartner, Gartner Sales Survey Finds 67% of B2B Buyers Prefer a Rep-Free Experience, March 2026. Survey of 646 B2B buyers, August to September 2025.

Next move

Calculate sales velocity for new business over the last 12 months, then again with no-decision losses included in the win rate. If the two figures differ by more than a fifth, your qualification stage needs a written exit rule.
